# origincloud_secret_manager_secret (Resource)

A secret: a name, the KMS key its payloads are encrypted under, and the versions that hold its value.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "origincloud_secret_manager_secret" "db" {
  project   = "my-project-123"
  region    = "eu-central1"
  secret_id = "billing-db-password"

  # Left out, the secret's payloads are encrypted under the project's default
  # Secret Manager key in the region. The key can't be changed afterwards.
  # kms_key = origincloud_kms_key.secrets.id

  tags = {
    team = "billing"
  }

  # Destroying a secret only schedules its deletion: it can be restored within
  # its recovery window, and its id stays taken until then. With force_delete
  # it is deleted at once, with all its versions, and the id is free again.
  # It is read from the state when the secret is destroyed, so apply it first.
  force_delete = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `project` (String) The project the secret is in. Changing it replaces the secret.
- `region` (String) The region the secret is in. Changing it replaces the secret.
- `secret_id` (String) The id of the secret, the last segment of its name: 1 to 63 characters, lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter (`[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,62}`), such as `billing-db-password`. It is how people and configuration refer to the secret, and it can't be changed. Anything else is refused with `BAD_REQUEST`. The secret's id, the last segment of its name. Changing it replaces the secret.

### Optional

- `force_delete` (Boolean) Whether destroying the secret deletes it and all of its versions at once, with no recovery window, which frees its `secret_id` for a new secret. Left out or `false`, destroying it only schedules the deletion: the id stays taken, and the API refuses a new secret with it until the recovery window has passed, or the secret is restored outside Terraform. Destroying reads this from the state, so apply a change to it before the apply that destroys the secret. It needs the permission to force-delete the secret. The API never returns it: an imported secret has none.
- `kms_key` (String) The full name of the KMS key every payload of the secret is encrypted under, `//kms.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/regions/{region}/keys/{key}`: an `ENCRYPT_DECRYPT` key of the secret's own project and region. Left out on CreateSecret, it is the project's default Secret Manager key in the region: a key the platform creates in your project with its first secret there that names no key, tagged `origin:name=secretmanager` and marked `platform_managed`, which you see in your KMS key list and audit log but can't change or delete. A key of another project or region, or a signing key, is refused with `BAD_REQUEST`. It can't be changed after the secret is created. While the key is disabled or deleted, AddSecretVersion and AccessSecretVersion are refused with `CONFLICT` naming it; once it is enabled again, they succeed again. Changing it replaces the secret.
- `tags` (Map of String) Labels of your own, at most 50. The `origin:name` tag is the name the console shows. Tags aren't secret: never put a secret value in one.

### Read-Only

- `create_time` (String) When the secret was created. An RFC 3339 timestamp, such as `2026-11-01T12:00:00Z`.
- `delete_time` (String) When the secret was deleted; unset unless it is `DELETED`. An RFC 3339 timestamp, such as `2026-11-01T12:00:00Z`.
- `expire_time` (String) When a deleted secret is destroyed with its versions, and its id becomes free; unset unless it is `DELETED`. RestoreSecret is refused after it. An RFC 3339 timestamp, such as `2026-11-01T12:00:00Z`.
- `id` (String) The secret's full resource name, `//secretmanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/regions/{region}/secrets/{secret}`: what an argument that refers to the secret takes. `name` is the relative name, without the host.
- `name` (String) The secret's resource name, `projects/{project}/regions/{region}/secrets/{secret}`. Its last segment is the `secret_id` given to CreateSecret.
- `state` (String) Whether the secret is in use or scheduled for deletion. One of `ACTIVE`, `DELETED`.
- `update_time` (String) When the secret last changed. An RFC 3339 timestamp, such as `2026-11-01T12:00:00Z`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A secret is imported by its full resource name, or its relative one.
terraform import origincloud_secret_manager_secret.db //secretmanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/my-project-123/regions/eu-central1/secrets/billing-db-password
```
